name: Kentucky

context: KY 340: Cover crops are meant to reduce sheet, rill, and wind erosion.
KY 329: Use RUSLE2 to set the surface residue needed, when it must be present, and how much soil disturbance is allowed.
cover_rules: KY 340: Do not burn cover crop residue.
KY 340: Do not mechanically harvest cover crop biomass; leave residues on the surface after termination.
residue: KY 345: For wind erosion, find the required height of standing residue after harvest, how long to keep it, and the row direction and ridge height.
KY 329: Pick tillage equipment that leaves enough aboveground residue in the periods with the highest erosion rates.
seeding: KY 327: Add 3 lbs. PLS of native grass to any wildlife forb mix.
KY 512: Warm-season grass rates are on a PLS basis.
pasture: KY 512: Optimum Ky bluegrass and orchardgrass seeding is 15 lbs./ac, 2/15-3/15 or 8/20 - 9/20.
disturbed: KY 528: Grazing management aims to prevent or reduce sheet, rill, classic gully, ephemeral gully, bank, or wind erosion.

cover.name: Barley, winter (black) oats, triticale or cereal rye

coverPlant.text: KY 340: Sow barley, winter (black) oats, triticale or cereal rye August 15th- October 15th.
KY 340: Cereal rye alone can go in November 15th-December 7th.

seedWin.text: KY 512: Cool-season grasses and legumes, optimum 2/15-3/15 in spring or 8/20 - 9/20 in fall.
